summary: Persistent 429s for interactive chat after enabling VPC egress via NAT with pooled ephemeral IPs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightChat reported sudden, sustained 429 responses for interactive chat calls after enabling VPC egress through their NAT gateway. Errors started ~2026-03-12 02:00 UTC coincident with a networking change (move to pooled ephemeral egress IPs).

Impact:
- ~25% of chat API calls returning 429 over HTTP/2 and websocket sessions for BrightChat users.
- Real-time UX degraded; customer reports timeouts and escalations to their engineering lead.
- Background embedding ingestion from the same VPC also observed token usage spikes.

Environment:
- Customer: BrightChat Inc. (private deployment, VPC egress to Redwood edge)
- Regions: us-west-2 (primary), traffic from same subnet NATted through shared ephemeral IP pool
- Models: redwood-chat-v1 pinned

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer starts interactive chat sessions concurrently with a background embedding ingestion job (low QPS per session, many concurrent sessions).
2) Both flows egress through the same NAT gateway that performs source IP pooling.
3) After NAT change, observed 429s within 1–3 minutes for interactive calls; bulk ingestion continued but contributed to quota burn.

Observed behavior:
- 429 response includes X-RateLimit-Reason: token_bucket_exhausted and X-RateLimit-Scope: per-ip + per-key.
- Edge logs show multiple distinct API keys and websocket sessions mapped to a small set of source IPs (NAT pooling).
- Rate-limit counters for those source IPs quickly hit the short-window burst limit.

Expected behavior:
- Interactive chat should be throttled by API key quotas primarily; source IP aggregation should not cause cross-customer or cross-key exhaustion in private VPC setups.

Attached logs / diagnostic snippets (sanitized):
- edge-proxy request sample: method=POST path=/v1/chat api_key=bKz*** src_ip=34.203.11.7 x-forwarded-for=10.0.2.45
- rate-limiter counter dump: ip_bucket[34.203.11.7].burst=500/500; api_key_bucket[bKz***].burst=320/1000
- NAT mapping snapshot (customer provided): 150 internal sessions -> 8 ephemeral public IPs
comments: 2026-03-12 02:08 UTC - BrightChat support: 'After we flipped the NAT pooling config, users started seeing chat failures — looks like 429s even though token usage is low per key.'
2026-03-12 02:22 UTC - Support (Juniper): 'Thanks — can you share a recent request id and confirm whether you run background embedding workers from the same VPC?'
2026-03-12 02:45 UTC - BrightChat support: 'Request id r-0a1b2c3d; yes, background workers on same subnet. We switched to pooled egress to save costs.'
2026-03-12 04:05 UTC - SRE (Ethan): 'Reproduced pattern in edge logs — many keys share the same public IP. We see rate-limiter incrementing against per-ip buckets leading to early exhaustion.'

2026-03-13 09:30 UTC - Support (Juniper): 'Hotfix deployed to edge proxy to prefer original client IP from X-Forwarded-For when upstream is on our trusted proxy list; also scoped per-ip accounting disabled for this tenant as mitigation.'
2026-03-14 11:12 UTC - BrightChat: 'Confirming errors dropped to <1% after hotfix and configuration change. UX restored.'
investigation_notes: Checked edge-proxy access logs (us-west-2) — pattern: large fanout of internal client IPs NATted to small ephemeral pool -> repeated increments to same per-ip token buckets.
Reviewed rate-limiter logic: currently enforces layered buckets (per-key AND per-source-ip). In VPC NAT scenarios, source-ip layer can be overly coarse and cause cross-key interference.

Hypothesis: NAT pooling turned many distinct customers/sessions into shared public IPs; with per-ip accounting enabled, short-window burst credits were exhausted by background jobs, producing 429s for interactive sessions.

Tested counter: artificially injected 200 concurrent small requests from separate internal IPs but same public IP — observed per-ip burst counter hitting limit while individual api_key buckets remained under threshold.

Checked trusted proxy list config: X-Forwarded-For was present but edge proxy had been configured to prefer egress IP for per-ip accounting when request arrived from known cloud NAT ranges — this policy caused misattribution in private VPCs.
Related GH PR created to make per-ip accounting opt-in for private customers and to tighten trust->client-ip derivation (see PR #3421).
root_cause: Per-IP rate limiting layer combined with NAT gateway IP pooling caused cross-session quota exhaustion. Edge proxy configuration used public egress IP for bucket attribution instead of original client IP (and per-ip accounting was enabled for the tenant), producing collateral 429s for interactive traffic.
resolution: Immediate mitigation (2026-03-12): disabled per-ip accounting for BrightChat tenant via feature flag; added temporary per-tenant exemption for source-ip buckets to restore chat traffic.

Short-term fix (2026-03-13): patched edge-proxy to prefer X-Forwarded-For when request originates from customer VPC ranges in the trusted-proxy list and to annotate requests with negotiated client_ip for rate-limiter.

Long-term remediation (deployed 2026-03-14): rate-limiter change to require both authentication and explicit per-ip opt-in before applying per-ip buckets; added observability dashboard for per-ip vs per-key bucket saturation and a runbook for VPC NAT scenarios.
Customer validation: BrightChat confirmed error rate returned to baseline (<1%). Monitoring kept on for 72 hours post-fix.
Code/links: GH PR https://github.com/redwoodinference/infra/pull/3421 merged; runbook updated at https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SUPPORT/NAT+IP+Pooling+Runbook
follow_up_actions: Create a small support KB entry describing VPC NAT pitfalls and recommended config (eg: separate egress for background ingestion or opt-in per-ip policy).
Add automated detection to console: if a private tenant's traffic shows >N api_keys mapped to <=M public IPs, surface a warning and suggested mitigations.
Schedule a postmortem with Networking and Rate-Limit owners to consider defaulting per-ip accounting off for private customers; target decision by 2026-04-01.
